narrative: Material PL1__M79A48C9 shows smooth, high-volume demand averaging 734 units/day with moderate CV of 0.32 and no statistically significant trend. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.81), dominated by transportation variance, requiring a substantial safety buffer of 1,180 units. An (r,Q) policy with order quantity capped at 5,056 units due to storage constraints consolidates 503 annual orders under SAP into just 36, delivering 86.5% annual cost reduction while maintaining 95% service level.
warnings: EOQ (6,464) exceeds available storage after safety stock; order quantity capped at 5,056 units due to max_storage_units=6,236.438 constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand with 100% non-zero fraction and high daily volume makes a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. The unstable lead time (CV=0.81) requires robust safety stock rather than safety lead time alone. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs; the capacity cap prevents storage overflow.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity is capacity-constrained (5,056 vs. unconstrained 6,464). This increases order frequency from the theoretical optimum, raising annual ordering cost by approximately 28% above the unconstrained EOQ minimum. Service level is maintained but total cost is slightly above the theoretical optimum.
